newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan '97 rubber demand for tyres seen a tad lower.
newsitem.headline: Japan '97 rubber demand for tyres seen a tad lower.

text.p: Japan's rubber demand for tyres is expected to decline by 0.8 percent in calendar 1997 to 1.06 million tonnes from estimated 1996 levels, the Automobile Tire Manufacturers Association said on Tuesday.
Japan rubber demand for tyres is expected to hit a record high of 1.068 million tonnes this year, helped by buoyant tyre demand for exports, the industry body said.

The association forecasts rubber demand for new cars will fall by 2.0 percent next year on a year-on-year basis to 206,000 tonnes due to an expected fall in domestic auto production, while demand for exports will slip by 1.7 percent to 432,000 tonnes.
Tyre demand for replacement purposes is expected to rise 0.8 percent to 422,000 tonnes in 1997, the industry body said.
"A scheduled rise in the domestic consumption tax from April next year will help slow domestic tyre demand for new cars," an official of the industry body said.
Tyre demand for exports could also slow down as large-lot orders from Middle Eastern countries, which boosted demand this year, are unlikely to come again next year, it said.
